compliance.environment: Indoor use only, in environmentally controlled areas

physical.material: Steel and aluminum with plastic T-shaped cable guides and plastic accessories

base.description: The manager as Chatsworth ships 32621-703, doors fitted, without accessories.

description: Motive double-sided vertical cable manager, Chatsworth Products 32621-703. It is a black steel and aluminum manager, 7 ft (2134 mm) tall and 8 in (200 mm) wide, with black fingers. It bolts to the side of the rack and stands beside it. Two channels stand back to back about a central track. Each has a T-shaped cable guide to every rack unit down both sides and a dual-hinged door. The overall depth is 23.6 in (600 mm). It takes no rack unit.

gaps.note: the data sheet's cable fill row points to the maker's cable fill table on its site and states no figure; that table is not held.
each door opens to the right or to the left and lifts off; the format has no hinge, so it is drawn as one fitted plate and the side it swings from is not stated.
gaps.wanted: a format that can say a hinged cover

gaps.note: no held page dimensions a guide: the arm, the head and the width are read by eye from the photographs and the page 2 figure.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side view of one guide

gaps.note: the data sheet says the guides align with rack units and gives no count; 48 a side on each face is the nominal 84 in over one rack unit.
gaps.wanted: the number of rack units the manager spans

gaps.note: the matrix prints the width (8 in) and the height (7 ft) as sizes to order by; only the depth is printed as an overall figure, so the width and the height are drawn at their nominal values.
gaps.wanted: an overall width and height, or a dimensioned drawing

gaps.note: only the overall depth is printed; the two channels and the centre section are each drawn a third of it less the doors (198), read from the proportions of the page 2 figure, which is not to a stated scale.

the data sheet and the installation drawing show an integral central track. No held page gives its width or how far it stands. The top and bottom faces draw it as a strip the full depth between the doors. The left and right faces draw the page 3 render's flat centre plate, 198 deep, in its place.

no held page dimensions a side assembly: it is drawn as a plate 1.5 thick under its guides, the length of the manager and the width of a guide, which is an estimate; the guides stand on it and in front of the central section.

the manager ships with four accessory rods, rotating fingers, cable bundle swivels and half spools (the data sheet, page 1; no fingers or spools on the 6 in and 8 in widths), which fit anywhere on the track; none has a fixed place, so none is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of a manager as shipped, with the accessories placed

gaps.note: the data sheet (page 6) sells a Mid Panel Kit. It covers and divides the front and rear of the double-sided manager. It is not part of the manager as shipped, so the kit's panel is not drawn. The flat centre plate of the page 3 render is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the manager as shipped

gaps.note: the data sheet (page 1, key features) names a hook on the inside of the front door for a test meter, in text only. The installation figure (page 3) shows a hinge lug and the rear door's latches, not a hook. No held picture shows the hook, so it is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the inside of the front door

gaps.note: the installation figure (page 3) shows four hinge tabs, one at each corner of the rear door's back. It also shows a central rib and two cross bars. It gives no size. They belong to the rear door's own part, which a following change draws, so they are not drawn here.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned view of the door's back

gaps.note: the end caps, feet and base plate show above and below the door in the data sheet's page 1 photograph. Each door plate is drawn to the full nominal height over the frame. It hides the fittings in the front and rear elevations. No held page gives the overall height with them.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned elevation with the caps and the feet

gaps.note: the page 1 photograph and the page 3 render show a row of rungs down the central track, seen through the open channel. The left and right faces draw the guides but not the rungs. The door plates hide the track in the front and rear elevations. No held page gives the pitch or size of a rung.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned view of the central track

gaps.note: each door is drawn as a flat plate 3 mm thick at the end of its channel; no held page gives its section. The frame, the guides and the door of each face stand in a well 201 deep, open behind.

the manager attaches to the rack with carriage bolts; how far it stands from the upright, where the rack's rails fall in the centre section and the rearward bias on a 3 in rack (installation instructions, page 2) are never dimensioned.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the manager fitted to a rack

gaps.note: the matrix says only Black; the shade drawn is read from the maker's renders of the fitted part, which no page gives as a colour value.

body.description: the frame of each face, the front and then the rear

door.description: the front door and then the rear door

guides.description: the T-shaped cable guides, the front face left side bottom to top and then right, then the rear face the same, 48 a side

attrs.note: datasheet - material, finish and the indoor-only statement are the specifications table (page 1): 'Steel and aluminum with plastic T-shaped cable guides and plastic accessories', 'Black or Glacier White powder coat paint'. The matrix (page 3) gives the colour of this part and its black fingers.

bottom.note: estimated - the bottom end has the layout of the top end: the doors, the channels and the centre section. It draws the base plate with four holes, two rails and four feet.

chassis.note: estimated - 200 mm wide, 2133.6 mm (7 ft, 84 in) high and 600 mm deep. THE DEPTH IS THE DATA SHEET'S (matrix note, page 3: 'Overall depth for Double-Sided manager is 23.6"D (600 mm)'); THE WIDTH AND THE HEIGHT ARE NOMINAL (matrix, page 3: 8" (200) and 7' (2.1)), taken here as the overall size, which the matrix does not say they are. The section is therefore estimated as a whole, and the figure of each dimension is in the entry that uses it.

color.note: estimated - 'Black' (matrix, page 3); the shade is the near-black of the data sheet's photographs of the fitted part, which are renders. The guides are black on every part number of this style.

door.note: estimated - the data sheet (page 1) lists a dual-hinged front door and a rear door assembly, pre-installed, and the installation instructions (page 3) draw the rear door as one plate; that the doors exist is printed, but no page prints a size of a door, so each is drawn as one plate of the manager's nominal width and height (the door components carry the method). A door opens to the right or to the left and lifts off; the format has no hinge, so the side is a gap. The front door has a latch tip at each edge and, on the 12 in width, two seams and a plate. The rear door is its own plain part with a latch tip at each edge. Each door has two latches on its inner face. On the side faces only the end of each handle shows, because the housing stands behind the arms. Each door component carries its figures.

fingers.note: estimated - A GUIDE TO EACH RACK UNIT, 48 A SIDE ON EACH FACE, 192 IN ALL. The data sheet (page 1) says the side assemblies carry T-shaped cable guides 'that align with rack-mount unit (U) spaces on rack'; no page counts them. 48 is the nominal 84 in over 1.75 in, a column from the foot to the top of the manager. A guide is an arm 12 high with a head 30 high and 20 wide, read by eye from the page 1 photographs and taken to be the same on every width and on both faces.

frame.note: estimated - the data sheet's page 1 photograph of the double-sided manager shows two caps on its top and two feet on a base plate. The data sheet's page 3 render shows four caps, a flat plate between the two channels and three feet. The other feet are inferred from the visible ones and the symmetry. No page gives a size. 12 scales are used, each in the direction it was read. Scale 1, photograph, read down: 2.624 mm per pixel, the nominal height 2133.6 mm over the left door's rows 72 to 885, 813 rows. Scale 2, photograph, read across: 2.679 mm per pixel, the 12 in width 300 mm over the door's columns at half level, 112 columns. Scale 3, photograph, read across: 10.3 mm per pixel, the depth 600 mm over the left face's columns 97 to 155, 58 columns. Scale 4, render, read across: 5.1 mm per pixel, the centre section 198 mm over the plate's columns, 39 columns. Scale 5, render, read across: 5.35 mm per pixel, the centre section 198 mm over the near plate's end columns 118 to 155, 37 columns. Scale 6, render, read along the width axis: 4.4 mm per pixel, the door's width 300 mm over the cap centres, 67.8 pixels. Scale 7, render, read along the depth axis: 3.7 mm per pixel, the depth 600 mm over the left rail, 162 pixels. Scale 8, render, read down: 4.267 mm per pixel, the nominal height 2133.6 mm over the render's rows, 500 rows. Scale 9, plan, read both: 0.7444 mm per pixel, the centre section 198 mm over its columns 552 to 818, 266 pixels. Scale 10, elevation, read across: 2.357 mm per pixel, the centre section 198 mm over its columns 2188 to 2272, 84 columns. Scale 11, elevation, read down: 1.374 mm per pixel, the nominal height 2133.6 mm over the manager's rows 515 to 2068, 1553 rows. Scale 12, elevation, read both: 1.484 mm per pixel, the plan's square 14.1 mm over the page 3 square's outline, 9.5 pixels. The centre section's 198 mm is itself an estimate, so scales 4, 5, 9 and 10 rest on it. The pictures are the data sheet's page 1 photograph and page 3 render, and the installation instructions' page 2 plan and page 3 elevation. Each figure below names its picture, the pixels it spans, its direction and its scale. A cap (page 1 photograph) is 28 columns across at 2.679 mm per pixel, so 75 wide. It is 8 rows down at 2.624 mm per pixel, so 21 tall. The cap and foot widths are read on the 12 in part and drawn on every width. A cap's depth is half its width, 37.5, a stand-in that no picture gives. A foot (page 1 photograph) is 22 columns across at 2.679 mm per pixel, so 58.9 wide. It is 5 rows down at 2.624 mm per pixel, so 13.1 tall. A foot's depth is half its width, 29.5, a stand-in that no picture gives. A render foot (page 3 render) is 7 columns across at 4.4 mm per pixel, so 30.8 wide. The render's feet are narrower than the photograph's, and the photograph rules at its finer scale. The base rim (page 1 photograph) is 3 rows down at 2.624 mm per pixel, so 7.9 tall. The bottom's base outline is the chassis width by its depth. A base-plate or side-plate hole (page 1 photograph) is 3 rows down at 2.624 mm per pixel, so 7.9 across. A side-plate dot (page 1 photograph) is 2 rows down at 2.624 mm per pixel, which gives 5.2 across, and 5 is drawn, within 0.3. A rail's width (page 3 render) is 15.25 rows down at 4.4 mm per pixel after the slant correction of 0.952, so 70.5 wide. The correction 0.952 is sin 29.1 plus sin 27.8, the angles read in the render. The base rails take the same width, because the door hides them in the render. The cross tube's depth (page 3 render) is 14.75 rows down at 3.7 mm per pixel, so 54.6 deep. The cross tube's place (page 3 render) is 44.3 percent of the way from the front cap centres to the rear ones, 556.5 mm apart. It is the mean of four readings along the cap centres: 45.4, 43.7, 45.5 and 42.6. The rear beam's depth (page 3 render) is 7 rows down at 3.7 mm per pixel, so 25.9 deep. The centre plate is the centre section, 198 deep, between the two channels. A rounded lower corner's radius (page 2 plan) is 17.5 rows down at 0.7444 mm per pixel, so 13 radius. The plate's rounded foot is three corner radii tall, 39. A tall base rail (page 2 plan) is 44 rows down at 0.7444 mm per pixel, so 32.8 tall. A round hole of the near plate (page 3 render) is 2.57 columns across at 5.1 mm per pixel, so 13.1 across. Its rows span 2.29 on average, 9.8 down, and the column reading is used. The far plate's dark hole (page 3 render) is 3 columns across at 5.1 mm per pixel, so 15.3 across. A slot (page 3 render) is 4 columns across at 5.1 mm per pixel, so 20.4 wide. It is 2 rows down at 4.267 mm per pixel, so 8.5 tall. A faint mark (page 3 render) is 1.5 columns across at 5.1 mm per pixel, so 7.7 across. A plan square (page 2 plan) is 19 columns across at 0.7444 mm per pixel, so 14.1 wide. It is 19 rows down at 0.7444 mm per pixel, so 14.1 tall. The plan slot (page 2 plan) is 35 columns across at 0.7444 mm per pixel, so 26.1 wide. It is 19 rows down at 0.7444 mm per pixel, so 14.1 tall. A plan screw ring (page 2 plan) is 20 columns across at 0.7444 mm per pixel, so 14.9 across. A page 3 square (page 3 elevation) is 9.5 columns across at 1.484 mm per pixel, so 14.1 wide. It is 9.5 rows down at 1.484 mm per pixel, so 14.1 tall. It is drawn at the plan square's size, so the scale of the page 3 marks is a transfer from the plan. The page 3 triangle (page 3 elevation) is 11 columns across at 1.484 mm per pixel, so 16.3 wide. It is 8 rows down at 1.484 mm per pixel, so 11.9 tall. The page 3 dot (page 3 elevation) is 5 columns across at 1.484 mm per pixel, so 7.4 across. The near plate's hole columns (page 3 render) are 37 columns across at 5.35 mm per pixel, so 198 in all. The head holes, the foot holes, the foot slots and the fifth dot stand at the columns the render shows. The near plate's slot and dot rows (page 3 render) are read down at 4.267 mm per pixel. Each row is counted from the render's foot line under it. The far plate's mark places (page 3 render) are read across at 5.1 mm per pixel. They are read down at 4.267 mm per pixel. A column is counted from column 56 and a row from row 75, and each row is corrected by 0.49 per pixel along the axis. The overlay marks (page 3 render) are read across at 5.35 mm per pixel. They are read down at 4.267 mm per pixel. An overlay of the render on the built plate gave two more rows of marks, near 200 mm and 861 mm, and a foot row. The plan's places (page 2 plan) are read across at 0.7444 mm per pixel. They are read down at 0.7444 mm per pixel. The plan gives four squares, a slot and four screws on the centre section. The page 3 marks' places (page 3 elevation) are 84 columns across at 2.357 mm per pixel, so 198 wide. They are 1553 rows down at 1.374 mm per pixel, so 2133.6 tall. Page 3 adds three pairs of squares, a triangle and a dot. The side plate's mark places (page 1 photograph) are read across at 10.3 mm per pixel. They are read down at 2.624 mm per pixel. A mark stands along the depth at 20 plus its column less 99.5, times 10.3, and down at its row less 72, times 2.624. The side plate shows four marks near 505 mm, two dots near 1904 mm and one near 219 mm. The side plate's three holes stand at depths 20, 82 and 124, 100 down. Two dots stand at depths 82 and 144, 1010 down. All five are read by eye from the photograph. The bottom's four plate holes stand 12 from the left edge and 40, 100, 145 and 285 from the rear door, read by eye. The foot holes' centres stand 60 above the plate's foot, an estimate. Each door is 3 thick, the door part's own figure, and the fittings stand inside it. The plan's lips and foot blocks lie beyond the 600 mm depth, where a face clips decor, so none is drawn. The front and rear doors paint over the fittings, so those faces show none.

front.note: estimated - the front channel with its door fitted. With the door off the front is the channel between the two side assemblies, the heads of the guides down each edge and the central track between them. The channel is 160 wide, the nominal 200 less a side assembly of 20 each side, which is an estimate.

guides.note: estimated - the duct on each face is the channel between the two side assemblies, 160 wide, run down the height (`run: y`). Its finger pitch is the rack unit, 44.45; the gap between arms is the pitch less the arm's estimated 12.

left.note: estimated - the side, rear at x=0: 48 arms and heads at one rack unit on each face and a door at each end. The side is open between the arms, as the data sheet's photographs show a side of slots. The flat centre plate of the page 3 render stands between the channels. Each door's latch stands on the door's inner face. The housing is 15 x 70.5 mm, 4.7 to 1, the proportion of the page 3 figure's housing. That housing is 18 x 85.5 px at 300 dpi. At the figure's 1.380 mm per px it is about 25 x 118 mm. The built size is a stand-in. The arms and heads stand in front of the housing. Only about 14 mm of each 45 mm handle shows, between two heads.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE DATA SHEET'S ORDERING MATRIX; THE CONSTRUCTION FROM ITS TEXT AND THE INSTALLATION DRAWINGS. The Motive Cable Management data sheet (MKT-60020-675, 09/24) (page 3) builds the part number 32621-703 from a style (2, double-sided, black fingers), a width (8 in, 200 mm), a colour (Black) and a height (7 ft), and prints one overall depth for a double-sided manager, 23.6 in (600 mm). THE WIDTH AND THE HEIGHT ARE NOMINAL: the matrix prints them as sizes to order by, not as overall dimensions, and the figures here are taken as the overall size. The page 1 specifications and the installation instructions (IIS-737610) say what the manager is made of and how it is mounted and fitted with its doors. NO HELD PAGE DIMENSIONS THE PART INTERNALLY: a guide, a side assembly, the track, the centre section and the door are estimated, each in its own entry below. The matrix figures are transcribed, not copied from a picture. The frame fittings are read from the pictures, and the `frame` entry lists them as a table. A row is one figure: its picture, the pixels it spans, the direction it is read in, the scale, the size drawn and the tolerance. The direction is down the rows or across the columns of that picture. The tolerance is how far the drawn size may differ from the pixels times the scale; it is 0.05 unless a row says otherwise. The scale list holds 12 scales, each the millimetres of a known part over the pixels it spans.

mount.note: drawing - rack-side. The installation instructions (page 2) have the manager positioned next to the rack and attached with 4 M8 carriage bolts, washers and flange nuts at the upper and lower pairs of holes, and draw the double-sided manager with the mounting holes of a 3 in and a 6 in wide rack in its centre section, so it stands beside the rack, outside the rails, a face to the front and a face to the rear. It occupies no rack unit; `ru: 48` is the 7 ft height over one rack unit and is estimated, because no held page says which racks a Motive height is for. The page 2 text says the manager is biased towards the rear on a 3 in wide rack; the model is drawn equal about its centre.

rear.note: estimated - the rear channel with its door fitted. The data sheet (page 1) lists a dual-hinged front door and rear door assembly, and the installation instructions (page 3) say the rear door is a plain flat door. No page draws the rear guides; the installation instructions' page 2 figure draws guides on both sides of the centre section and the rear is taken to be the front again, 48 a side.

right.note: estimated - the left view mirrored: the manager is the same on both sides, except the centre plate's head. The render's far plate shows its own head pattern, drawn on this face. The rear end is on the right in this view. The rear latch and the rear guides stand there, and the front ones stand at the left.

shell.note: drawing - a hollow manager, as every manager in the library is. The body is a sheet body and its views are elevations; the solid is what its parts build: a frame and the guides on each face, and the two doors that lift off.

spine.note: estimated - the centre section, 198 deep between the two channels, with the central track and the mounting holes for the rack (installation instructions, page 2). The page 2 figure draws the rear guides, the centre and the front guides about equal in depth, so each is a third of the overall depth less the doors. The figure is not to a stated scale. The data sheet (page 6) sells a Mid Panel Kit that 'covers and divides the front and rear'. That kit is a separate part and is not drawn. The flat centre plate of the page 3 render is drawn between the channels, with its holes and slots, in the side views.

thickness.note: estimated - no held page states a wall gauge. 1.5 is the plate of comparable parts in the library; the parts carry their own thicknesses.

top.note: estimated - the end of the manager seen from above, rear at y=0: a door 3 thick at each end, a channel of 198 at each, and the centre section of 198 between. The 600 is the data sheet's; the split is the estimate of the centre section, the guide and the frame. It draws four end caps, two rails, a cross tube and a beam across the rear. The cross tube stands 44 percent of the way from the front caps to the rear caps.
